imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer in the rough searches for his ball among trees and then prepares to replay his previous shot from the original spot with his iron.
imageAlt: A boy golfer looks for a lost ball in the trees and walks back to replay his shot.

issues: The scene lacks a strong indication of deep rough or dense trees, making it look closer to semi-rough than a truly 'lost ball' scenario.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Increase the thickness and density of the rough grass slightly, and add more prominent and closer trees in the background and sides to create a sense of a challenging search area. Keep all other details the same.

questions.title: What happens if you lose your ball?
questions.question: You hit your ball into the trees and look for it for 4 minutes, but can't find it. What should you do now?

choices.text: Drop a ball near where it went missing and keep playing without a penalty
Keep looking for as long as you want until you find your ball
Go back to where you last hit your shot, drop a new ball within one club-length, and add one extra shot
Start playing a new ball from any spot you like on the course

questions.explanation: If you can’t find your ball after looking for 3 minutes, it is called a lost ball. You must go back to where you last hit your shot, drop a ball within one club-length, and count one extra shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The length of your golf club. When dropping a ball, you can drop it within this distance from a set spot.
An extra shot you have to add to your score when you break a rule.
When you can't find your ball after looking for 3 minutes.

questions.teachingTip: Remind children to remember how long they are allowed to look for their ball and to know where they last hit their shot.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they can keep looking for their ball as long as they want.
They may believe they can drop a ball anywhere if their ball is lost.

questions.title: What counts as a lost ball?
questions.question: You hit your ball deep into the trees and spend 4 minutes searching but can't find it. What must you do under the Rules?

choices.text: Drop a ball near where it disappeared with no penalty
Continue searching until you find it
Go back to where you last played, drop a ball within one club-length, and add one penalty stroke
Play a new ball from anywhere you like

questions.explanation: If you cannot find your ball within three minutes, it is lost. You must return to where you last played, drop a ball within one club-length, and take a one-stroke penalty.
